source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 29:1 binds Hebrew 28:69; public 29:2–29 binds Hebrew 29:1–28. All other public verses in chapters 27–34 align directly. All 266 original XML records, including written/read and numbering notes, are hashed in full.

key_decisions.decision: Follows the pinned holy-myriad wording and recorded two-word read form fiery law, while flagging the obscure final line.
Retains peoples and his/your shifts; selects bow for the rare verb and distributes the singular receiving action.
Keeps the unnamed he and Jeshurun, leaving the king’s identity open in the text.
Does not insert a second not before few; renders the compact final clause concessively and records the alternative.
Preserves Thummim/Urim order and the unnamed faithful man, with testing/contention wordplay noted.
Uses the contextual regard sense of not seeing parents, follows read plural sons, and keeps the shift to they.
Preserves the bodily violence and the repeated rise contrast alongside blessing and acceptance.
Keeps the intimate protection image and source pronouns without asserting a certain identification of every he/him.
Retains bush-dweller and head/crown imagery without turning set apart into a formal Nazirite vow.
Preserves bull and wild-ox images, goring violence, and the unequal Ephraim/Manasseh numbers.
Preserves the unnamed mountain, righteous sacrifices, and striking suckling-from-seas image.
Keeps the blessing’s recipient as Gad’s enlarger and preserves the violent lion image and both body parts.
Keeps the obscure ruler’s reserved portion without identifying it as Moses’ grave, and retains the justice claims.
Chooses west for the sea/west term while retaining south and noting the geographical alternative.
Keeps the among-sons reading and the abundance image of a foot dipped in oil.
Selects bars and strength for two uncertain terms, retaining both metals and the days comparison.
Preserves ancient God, dwelling, arms, and the explicit destructive command without conjectural replacement.
Retains the spring-of-Jacob image and the source’s alone term, with agricultural abundance.
Preserves shield and sword, enemy submission, and pinned high places rather than substituting backs.
